summary: No strong candidate. Code reading of crisium.lua, prt-epoch.lua, prt-bridge.lua (observe/jobs/tick), prt-log-history.lua, the stored player's epoch hand-off in prt.lua, DaveConsensus.sol and Tournament.sol finished/standing logic, plus one end-to-end run on the local chain with the patched Dave build, found the player assigning inputs to epochs as DaveConsensus does in every case tried, apart from the cases already confirmed (R1-A3-1 backlog, R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-2 epoch 0). The two candidates below are weak.

candidates.title: Verification-game recipe (vg.lua) caps an epoch at 2^16 inputs, while the manual's verification game and the emulator's dispute constant use 2^24
candidates.component: Verification-game referee and honest player in doc/recipes/vg.lua (the manual's 'Verification game' section)
candidates.role: Support (referee and player of the verification game, not the PRT referee model). Rated as support standing in for a referee or operator.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/vg.lua:21 (LOG2_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH = 16), :24 (INPUTS_PER_EPOCH), :928 (settle_dispute extent log2_input_count), :1030 (new_dapp_contract assert #input_paths <= INPUTS_PER_EPOCH); doc/README.md:9448 ('Within the maximum number of inputs per epoch (2^24)') and :9565 (snippet using LOG2_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH)
candidates.description: The manual's verification-game section says the state transition grid has a maximum of 2^24 inputs per epoch, which is cartesi.ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH = 24, the dispute constant that DaveConsensus (MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH) and prt.lua use. vg.lua hard-codes LOG2_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH = 16 instead of using the emulator constant. Its referee bisects over an input extent of 2^16, and new_dapp_contract refuses by assert any epoch with more than 65,536 inputs. So for an input record that a 2^24 deployment accepts (65,537 to 2^24 inputs per epoch), the verification-game referee cannot adjudicate the epoch, and its honest player cannot defend it. This is a mismatch with the manual and the deployment's input limit, not a soundness issue: past the last input the state is unchanged, so with up to 2^16 inputs both grids give the same final state.
candidates.trigger: Anyone who sends more than 65,536 inputs in one epoch of an application that the verification-game recipe referees (InputBox inputs are permissionless).
candidates.reachability: Reachable whenever an epoch holds more than 2^16 inputs, which A3 allows up to 2^24.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion fits. The trigger is input count, which section 7 gives the adversary ('Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts'). 2 Role: vg.lua is not the PRT referee model of section 5 ('The manual's permissionless refereed tournament is the normative model'), so per AUDIT.md it is support (a demonstration referee and operator). 3 High/Medium: in the role it stands in for (a referee, or an honest operator that must 'assign inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3)', R4), refusing an epoch is at most a stall of the model. Section 3 says a defect that 'only crashes or stalls the model ... is rated as support'. 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual is right, the vg honest player cannot defend an epoch the deployment forms, which is an R4 violation in the stood-in honest role. A support defect that stands in for a Critical one rates Medium, and a stall-only reading rates Low. 4/5: Medium under the stood-in-operator reading, Low under the model-stall reading.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Medium if the vg player is read as standing in for an honest operator that must defend every epoch of up to 2^24 inputs)
candidates.threat_to_goal: None for PRT/Dave deployments. A deployment that settled disputes with the verification game as the manual describes it would leave epochs of more than 2^16 inputs undefended and unrefereed.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only. vg.lua:21 vs cartesi.ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH = 24 and the manual text at doc/README.md:9448.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test that loads vg.lua as a module and calls vg.new_dapp_contract(hash, inputs) with 2^16+1 placeholder input paths (small files, or a stubbed fs.read_file), asserting that it does not raise. Alternatively assert that the extent the referee uses equals cartesi.ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH. It exits 1 today.

candidates.title: crisium exits by assert and crash-loops forever once an epoch's winning final state cannot be staged (final state not an accepted yield)
candidates.component: PRT bridge and player process in doc/recipes (prt-bridge.lua prepare 'stageTournamentResult', crisium.lua main loop)
candidates.role: Support (the PRT player and bridge; AUDIT.md: 'No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI'), standing in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua:538-547 (pcall(eth.validity_proof) failure sets self.terminal); doc/recipes/crisium.lua:316 and :373 (assert(not status.terminal)); prt-supervise.sh relaunches it
candidates.description: When the root winner, the honest claim, settles a final state that is not a manual yield with the accepted reason (the guest halted, yielded manually with another reason, or stopped at imcyclemax in the epoch), validate_outputs_merkle_root_response fails. The bridge then sets terminal, and crisium asserts after the pass. Under prt-supervise.sh it relaunches, reopens the epoch, prepares the stage job again and exits again, forever. Jobs sorted after the stage job in the same tick (tryRecoveringBond, whose key sorts after stageTournamentResult) can still be published before the exit, so bond recovery eventually happens. Nothing else in the process runs normally again: no listener or bridge outlives the next pass, and the status file always reports terminal. Because Dave cannot stage such an epoch, no later epoch is ever sealed.
candidates.trigger: A guest, whether or not its application is correctly designed, ends an epoch in a state that is not an accepted yield, for example an input that makes it halt. Any input sender can trigger this for an application that an input can subvert.
candidates.reachability: Reachable: halting or yielding with any reason is guest behavior from any valid template (section 4: 'Any input may take control of ... the application').
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: section 8 excludes 'The stall of an application that halts, yields manually with a reason other than accepted or rejected, or never yields, and what the application loses by it. A5 governs what can then be extracted from its state.' The tournament is already decided for the honest claim before the stage job is prepared, so no open dispute is left undefended. What remains lost is the process's liveness and the application's progress. Under this reading it is out of scope. 2 Role: support standing in for the honest operator. 3/4: if read against R4 ('This holds for every guest, whether or not its application is correctly designed' and section 8: 'An application that breaks the rollup interface may leave its outputs unprovable, but it must never stop the honest operator from computing claims or producing proofs. Development tools may instead stop and report the violation'), the operator stops permanently. But in Dave no later dispute can open, so nothing more needs defending. 5 Low at most.
candidates.claimed_severity: Out of scope (application stall); Low otherwise
candidates.threat_to_goal: No settled state or output is affected. The only effect is a permanently crash-looping operator process for a stalled application.
candidates.evidence: Code reading. R2 DFCHAIN listed this path as not covered.
candidates.test_idea: Unit-level: drive a prt-bridge instance with a player whose prove_outputs_merkle_root returns the proof of a halted machine, call tick, and assert that the bridge reports the non-stageable epoch as an anomaly or a finished state instead of setting terminal, which crisium turns into an exit.

checked_no_candidate: Epoch partitioning in crisium/prt-epoch against DaveConsensus. The listener of epoch N runs from EpochSealed(N-1) to EpochSealed(N) and keeps inputs with index in [upper(N-1), upper(N-1)+2^24) in log order before EpochSealed(N). DaveConsensus samples upper(N) at accept(N-1), the same transaction as EpochSealed(N). So every input logged before EpochSealed(N) has index < upper(N) or past the cap, and every input after it has index >= upper(N). The seal's bounds are asserted against the listener's view.

Inputs in the sealing block, run on chain: a third party (not a validator) sent addInput, acceptStagedTournamentResult(0) and addInput in one block (tx indices 0, 1, 2). EpochSealed(1) bounds were 0..2: the earlier input went to epoch 1 and the later one to epoch 2. Both honest validators assigned them the same way and settled.
Empty epochs (0, 3, 4, 5) staged and accepted, with the honest checkpoints equal to the settled initialMachineStateHash and outputsMerkleRoot.

Downtime: a second honest validator (own state and checkpoints) was stopped during epoch 1 while validator a settled epochs 1-3. It was relaunched at epoch 4's seal, caught up epochs 1-3 from its stored epoch directories and the chain, and played epoch 4. Its epoch-4/5 checkpoints match the chain. Duplicate commitments (both validators joining the same claim) are handled: one join's preflight reverts and the claim binds to the commitment already joined.

Two open disputes at once cannot happen in Dave. A root reaches ROOT_WINNER only with matchCount == 0. A sealed inner match is deleted only through winInnerTournament (child WINNER, so finished) or eliminateInnerTournament (child ELIMINABLE, so finished). So no leaf match of epoch N is live when accept(N) moves provideMerkleRootOfInput's bounds, which confirms round 1's note that this is harmless.

Hand-off between epochs. The checkpoint's outputs_root is the tx-buffer word of the final machine, the same word LibMachineValidityProof extracts. After a rejected last input the final machine is the reverted, canonical state. The next epoch reloads the checkpoint with clear_hash_tree. Mismatches between the frontier and the tx buffer only report anomalies.

Sealing races. Someone else staging or accepting first makes the honest stage/accept preflight revert with code 3, and the job disappears once EpochStaged/EpochSealed(N+1) is observed. Cross-epoch nonce sharing in methods:tick: newest epoch first, another epoch's candidate is left alone. Cancel candidates carry no context, which only lets the current epoch replace them.
prt-log-history inclusive first block (fetched = first_block - 1), and the rewind/common-ancestor logic for the listener ranges.
not_covered: A backlog of more than 2^24 pending inputs (R1-A3-1 territory) and apps created apart from their DaveConsensus (R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-2) were not re-run.

The released Dave geometry and clocks (log2step 38, COMMITMENT_BUDGET 120 min, root allowance from censorship seconds) under the honest player's finality lag plus the synchronous run of pending inputs at epoch_sealed: an A7 sizing question, not quantified. The chain run used the patched geometry and anvil.

Idle starvation: crisium runs later-epoch inputs only when a pass finishes within one block. On fast chains, or when a pass exceeds the block time (R1-BOUNDARY growth), the next epoch's inputs all run synchronously at its seal. Noted, not measured.
Foreclosure during an open dispute: stage/accept preflights revert every tip, so jobs are retried forever. Not run.

Dave clock edge cases that could delete a sealed inner match while its child is live (a paused clock with zero allowance making eliminateMatchByTimeout classify ELIMINATE_BOTH). Only partly read; A7/A8 territory.
The sentinel's multi-epoch behaviour, and scripted adversaries across several epochs.
Stage by a third party with a valid proof (only third-party accept was exercised).
Chain reorganizations within the input policy around a seal (out of scope beyond finality) and Arbitrum/OP block-number semantics.
The Rust/sling node and the Cartesi Rollups Node (out of scope).

experiment.scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r4/RGEPOCHS/run.sh and scenario.lua (patched Dave on anvil port 8561, two honest crisium validators)
experiment.result: all checks passed (exit 0). The 'connection refused' relaunch lines in the saved player logs come after the scenario: the scratch script's os.exit skipped the supervisor cleanup (since fixed), and the supervisors were killed by hand. The 4 GB run directory was deleted.
